test_cases.name: explain_a_topic
test_cases.input: Explain what an IEP is and why it matters
assertions: Opens with one plain sentence that answers the question
Gives a concrete example before the definition
Uses short chunks, not a long paragraph
Separates goal from accommodation
Ends by repeating the key point in one sentence
Includes one textbook-style image with a one-sentence caption
Does not announce the user's disabilities

test_cases.name: number_problem
test_cases.input: My car payment is $1000 a month and I want it near $700. How much is that difference over a year?
assertions: States the result with the unit and what it means in words
Shows each calculation step on its own line
Does not skip the arithmetic or say just subtract
Ends with the key point in one sentence

test_cases.name: writing_task
test_cases.input: Help me email my professor that I need more time on the policy paper
assertions: Provides a copy-paste draft instead of asking the user to write a paragraph
Keeps the draft short
Labels any blanks the user might change
Does not talk down
Does not shrink the assignment unless asked

test_cases.name: adhd_start
test_cases.input: I keep not starting the module. Help me start.
assertions: Names one job only
Gives a first step small enough to do now
Does not add a second task
Does not shame them for not starting

test_cases.name: k12_504
test_cases.input: My 4th grader has trouble starting work. What goes on a 504 plan?
assertions: Treats the learner as K-12, not college
Says a 504 is access in the regular class, not special instruction
Lists specific supports such as written directions, chunked work, or a quiet room
Does not say an IEP does not exist for this child
Does not invent a diagnosis

test_cases.name: college_no_transfer
test_cases.input: Can I use my old IEP at my college?
assertions: Says the IEP does not transfer
Points them to disability services
Does not tell them to skip registering
